title: job-statement template variables
description: Values for templates/job-statement.md.j2 and templates/job-statement.html.j2. Generated by tpl-jinja from job-statement.md; `description` on each property is the question put to the author.

date.title: Date
date.description: "" — interview ,. From section '({} verbatim quotes from real switchers; minimum 3)'.

evidence_count.title: Evidence count
evidence_count.description: How many verbatim quotes from real switchers back this. Below three it is a hypothesis - write the number rather than an impression, and let the reader weigh it.

id.title: Id
id.description: "" — interview. From section '({} verbatim quotes from real switchers; minimum 3)'.

job_name.title: Job name
job_name.description: The product or feature this statement is scoped to. One job per statement - a job that covers your whole product is a mission statement wearing JTBD clothes.

motivation.title: Motivation
motivation.description: What they want to do in that moment, in their words and never in your feature's. "Get paid without damaging the relationship", not "send an automated reminder".

obvious_competing_products.title: Obvious competing products
obvious_competing_products.description: Direct. From section 'Competitive Set (same job, different solutions)'.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: The result they are after, functional and emotional together. The functional half explains what they bought; the emotional half explains why they finally switched after two years of coping.

quote.title: Quote
quote.description: The quote used under '({} verbatim quotes from real switchers; minimum 3)'.

situation.title: Situation
situation.description: The circumstance that makes this job live, emotional context included - "when the invoice is three weeks late and I have to email a client I like". This is the half people skip and the half that predicts switching.

success_metric.title: Success metric
success_metric.description: How the customer knows the job is done - their signal, not your dashboard. If only you can see it, you have written a product metric and called it a job.
